description: Does the Phoenix South 1 oil represent an extension of the Lower Triassic petroleum system of the Perth Basin? is a dataset listed in Australian national open data portal, an open data portal, published or maintained by Geoscience Australia Data. In 2014, the surprise discovery of oil in the well Phoenix South 1 on Australia’s North West Shelf (NWS) heralded the Bedout Sub-basin as Australia’s new petroleum province. The well had initially targeted gas in Triassic reservoirs of the Keraudren Formation and Locker Shale but unexpectedly encountered oil instead. Coverage: Australia. The portal files it under the publisher Geoscience Australia Data. Its tags are Organic Geochemistry, Petroleum, Published_External, Roebuck Basin. It offers 2 resource(s) in PDF. The portal shows 2025-10-16 as the last metadata change. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the portal listing (dataset page not read). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support fuel supply studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-ckan-au-portal.
